attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: 'We can safely expect' is a firm expectation, so it is scored. 'Reports like these' means reports that agents are brittle, and the horizon is the rest of 2025. Both are kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (many public reports of agent failures spread across 2025) is fair and ordinary. 'Many, many' has no count, but the support condition is reasonable.

evidence.note: April 2025 hands-on report that ChatGPT Tasks was unreliable.
May 2025 benchmark showing large agent failure rates on business tasks.
June 2025 Gartner view, carried by Reuters, that agents are immature and cannot follow nuanced instructions.
July 2025 widely covered report of the Replit agent deleting a production database.

reviews.rationale: The horizon ended 2025-12-31. Independent reports from news outlets, a benchmark and an analyst firm, spread from April to July 2025, document agent brittleness and failures. That fits 'many more reports throughout the year' on the plain reading. No counterevidence shows agents being reported as broadly reliable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The firm 'not this year, or next, or the one after that' refers back to agents doing a huge fraction of knowledge work. The hedged 'probably not this decade' is correctly left out. The narrow-use-case exception is kept.

contract.note: Reading 'huge fraction' as a large economy-wide share is ordinary. The early rule allows only contradiction, which is fair because the window runs to the end of 2027.

evidence.note: October 2025 benchmark: agents automated about 2.5% of remote work projects. This is consistent with the forecast so far but cannot settle a window that ends in 2027.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 2027-12-31, after the evaluation date. No evidence shows agents doing a large share of knowledge work broadly, so the early contradiction rule is not met. The forecast cannot be supported before its deadline.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' with 'eventually (no time soon)'. 'Maybe physical labor' is hedged and correctly left out of the test. Being worth trillions is tied to doing a huge share of knowledge work.

contract.note: An undated long-term forecast. Allowing early support only, with no early contradiction, is fair to 'no time soon'. 'Worth trillions' is ambiguous, but that does not matter for the current result.

evidence.note: Late-2025 benchmark showing agents automate little real work. This fits 'no time soon' but does not bear on 'eventually'.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given and the early support rule is not met: there is no evidence of agents doing a huge share of knowledge work or being worth trillions. Near-term weakness cannot contradict 'eventually'. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, about OpenAI's Tasks feature.

semantics.note: 'And it won't' is a firm forecast that ChatGPT Tasks scheduling will not work reliably. No horizon was stated.

contract.note: The result depends on reading 'reliably' as 'users could not count on tasks firing correctly'. That is an ordinary plain reading. The early rule (an independent hands-on test plus repeated user reports) is reasonable, though the evidence is anecdotal.

evidence.note: April 2025 independent hands-on review: a task fired 12 hours late and tasks were overwritten.
User reports on OpenAI's forum, January and August 2025, of tasks never running. These are user posts, not company disclosures.
December 2025 forum report that scheduled tasks did not run at all, showing the problems persisted.

reviews.rationale: The early resolution rule is met. An independent hands-on review documents wrong-time firing and overwritten tasks, and repeated user reports through December 2025 show tasks not running. No evidence shows near-flawless scheduling. The evidence is anecdotal; there is no systematic failure rate.
